headline: The blood marker improved. The trial failed.
summary: Follow CETP from human genetics and preclinical evidence into clinical testing, failure, later interpretation and the target class's current status.
relationship_note: This timeline starts with human genetics and target-level preclinical evidence, then follows the compound into clinical trials and later genetic reinterpretation. Early evidence supported CETP's effect on HDL and the target rationale; it did not establish torcetrapib safety or clinical benefit.

sections.title: The question
sections.text: If a drug improves HDL cholesterol, will it protect patients from coronary events? And if it fails, is the problem the blood marker, the target, or the particular drug?

sections.title: Retrieved MR: inspect the design
sections.text: The selected MVP1 HDL–CAD row has a negative pre-computed estimate. It remains visible beside the later curated literature. Different instruments, populations and endpoints can lead to different conclusions; a source p-value does not resolve these differences.

sections.title: A target-matched example: CETP
sections.text: CETP is an author-prioritized HDL gene in the project atlas. Torcetrapib and evacetrapib inhibit the CETP protein. This gives a real gene-to-drug link, while the atlas annotation alone does not prove mediation.

sections.title: What failed?
sections.text: Torcetrapib was stopped after excess mortality and cardiovascular events. Evacetrapib was stopped for insufficient efficacy. These are different failure modes and are shown as separate drug histories.

sections.title: What genetics adds
sections.text: Comparing CETP gene variants with torcetrapib helped distinguish lipid changes from the drug's blood-pressure effect. HDL-focused MR also challenged the assumption that raising this marker must prevent heart attacks.

sections.title: Keep the counterevidence
sections.text: This is not proof that genetic analysis would have predicted every failure, or that CETP is an invalid target. REVEAL found benefit with anacetrapib, and target-specific genetic analyses point to apoB-related effects.

sections.title: The target's story continues
sections.text: A retrieved PREVAIL record lists obicetrapib as Phase 3, active not recruiting; its last update is June 2024. A January 2026 sponsor update discusses continued development. Neither record is a completed cardiovascular-outcome result.

sections.title: What remains unresolved
sections.text: The selected baseline has no queried colocalisation or gene-QTL evidence. Source CI bounds include zero despite a small reported p-value; the CI level and scale are unspecified, so these fields are flagged rather than silently repaired. No claim of causal confidence is made from State A.

events.title: Torcetrapib raises HDL
events.description: A short multidose study showed that torcetrapib inhibited CETP and raised HDL in healthy participants.
events.scope: Compound-specific early human evidence; publication month

events.title: ILLUMINATE begins
events.description: Trial of torcetrapib plus atorvastatin versus atorvastatin in a coronary-risk population.
events.scope: Trial record; start date has month precision

events.title: Development stopped
events.description: Pfizer announced termination of ILLUMINATE and the compound's development after a mortality and cardiovascular-event imbalance.

events.title: Higher HDL, more harm
events.description: Published trial results showed improved lipid levels alongside higher mortality and cardiovascular morbidity.

events.title: Target or drug effect?
events.description: CETP genetic variants resembled the drug's lipid effects but not its blood-pressure rise, supporting an off-target explanation of that effect.

events.title: HDL assumption questioned
events.description: Some genetic mechanisms raising HDL did not lower heart-attack risk. This challenges HDL elevation as a sufficient rationale; it is not a CETP-specific negative result.
events.scope: Related later evidence; not a 2006 prediction

events.title: Another CETP drug shows benefit
events.description: REVEAL found fewer major coronary events with anacetrapib, showing that torcetrapib's failure did not invalidate the whole target class.

events.title: CETP development continues
events.description: A sponsor update described continued obicetrapib development; this is not a completed cardiovascular-outcome result.

sources.note: Author-prioritized gene annotation for HDL cholesterol, ENSG00000087237. The present atlas is not evidence available to a 2006 decision-maker.

sources.title: Inherited CETP deficiency (1989)
sources.note: A CETP splice-site mutation caused inherited CETP deficiency and markedly increased HDL. This establishes human genetic effects on the biomarker, not protection from coronary disease.

sources.title: CETP suppression in rabbits (1998)
sources.note: Target-level preclinical evidence: CETP antisense treatment reduced atherosclerotic lesions in cholesterol-fed rabbits. This was not a torcetrapib experiment.

sources.title: CETP inhibitor in rabbits (2000)
sources.note: A different CETP inhibitor, JTT-705, improved lipids and attenuated rabbit atherosclerosis. It supports the target class, not torcetrapib-specific safety or efficacy.

sources.title: Torcetrapib Phase 1 study (2004)
sources.note: Early human proof of mechanism: torcetrapib increased HDL over 14 days. Publication date is shown; the study began earlier, but no verified start date is asserted here.

sources.title: ILLUMINATE registry
sources.location: protocolSection identification, status, design and eligibility
sources.note: Phase 3 torcetrapib/atorvastatin versus atorvastatin. Population includes coronary heart disease or high-risk diabetes; broader than the exact CAD GWAS population.

sources.title: Pfizer programme stop (2006)
sources.note: Sponsor stopped trials and compound development after the mortality/cardiovascular-event imbalance.

sources.title: ILLUMINATE results (2007)
sources.location: Abstract and discussion; published online 2007-11-05; PMID 17984165
sources.note: Torcetrapib increased HDL but increased mortality and cardiovascular morbidity. This does not isolate CETP inhibition as the cause of harm.

sources.title: CETP genetics versus torcetrapib (2009 online)
sources.note: Genetic lipid effects resembled treatment; blood-pressure effects did not. Supports an off-target interpretation of the hypertensive effect, not proof of every cause of death.

sources.title: HDL cholesterol and heart attack MR (2012)
sources.note: Some genetic mechanisms raising HDL did not lower myocardial-infarction risk. HDL-level evidence is not a CETP-specific verdict; MI is related to, but not identical to, the CAD dataset outcome.

sources.title: ACCELERATE registry
sources.location: protocolSection identification, status, design and eligibility
sources.note: Phase 3, terminated for insufficient efficacy. High-risk vascular population and composite endpoint, not an exact reproduction of the CAD GWAS.

sources.title: Lilly programme stop (2015)
sources.note: Development for high-risk ASCVD discontinued due to insufficient efficacy; the stated stop was not for safety findings.

sources.title: ACCELERATE results (2017)
sources.location: Abstract and trial results; 2017-05 (month precision); PMID 28514624
sources.note: Favorable lipid changes did not translate into fewer cardiovascular events in this trial.

sources.title: CETP/HMGCR genetic analysis (2017)
sources.note: Cardiovascular associations tracked apoB reduction in the joint genetic analysis. Do not reduce CETP effects to HDL elevation alone.

sources.title: REVEAL anacetrapib results (2017)
sources.note: Anacetrapib reduced major coronary events in REVEAL. Necessary counterexample to a claim that all CETP inhibition fails.

sources.title: Obicetrapib PREVAIL registry
sources.location: protocolSection status and design; source update 2024-06-04
sources.note: Retrieved Phase 3 ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING record. Old registry update, not proof of current recruitment or programme-wide regulatory status.

sources.title: NewAmsterdam 2026 programme update
sources.note: Reports continuing obicetrapib development. Projections are not achieved outcomes; no global approval status is established here.

current_status.trial_description: A Study Examining Torcetrapib/Atorvastatin And Atorvastatin Effects On Clinical CV Events In Patients With Heart Disease
current_status.regulatory: Safety stop announced by Pfizer after excess deaths and cardiovascular events.
current_status.programme_status: Latest programme decision retrieved for this example; no exhaustive global revival/approval search.
